title: Air India Deploys New Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on Toronto Route, Cuts Travel Time by Three Hours
excerpt: The airline will eliminate the Vienna fuel stop on Delhi-Toronto flights from August 1, restoring daily service and debuting Premium Economy in Canada.
body:
• Air India will deploy its new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi-Toronto route from August 1, eliminating the Vienna fuel stop and cutting westbound travel time from approximately 20 hours to 17 hours.
  • Daily service between Delhi and Toronto will resume after a temporary reduction to five weekly flights during June and July due to high fuel prices.
  • Premium Economy debuts on Air India's Canadian routes, with the aircraft configured in three classes: 30 Business suites, 28 Premium Economy seats, and 238 Economy seats.
  • The deployment is part of a broader fleet renewal involving 600 new aircraft orders, with more than half of Air India's widebody fleet expected to feature new or upgraded cabins by end of 2026.

Air India will introduce its factory-new Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner on the Delhi-Toronto route beginning August 1, bringing the airline's latest cabin products to Canada for the first time and eliminating a fuel stop that has added hours to the westbound journey.

The new aircraft will allow the airline to drop the technical refuelling stop in Vienna on flights from Delhi to Toronto, cutting travel time from roughly 20 hours to around 17 hours, according to the airline. The Toronto-Delhi return leg already operates nonstop and will continue at a block time of approximately 16 hours. The removal of the fuel stop remains subject to available airspace.

Daily Flights Resume After Summer Reduction

Alongside the aircraft upgrade, Air India will restore daily service on the route after temporarily reducing frequencies to five weekly flights in June and July. The airline attributed the reduction to unprecedented fuel price increases and broader geopolitical challenges affecting flight operations.

"Canada is home to one of the world's largest and most vibrant Indian diaspora communities, and Toronto has long been one of Air India's most important international gateways."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO & Managing Director, Air India

Wilson added that the 787-9 deployment on the Toronto route "marks another important milestone" in Air India's transformation, extending its most premium offerings across North America.

The daily schedule from August 1 has Flight AI187 departing Delhi at 1:45 a.m. local time and arriving in Toronto at 9:30 a.m., while Flight AI188 departs Toronto at 12:30 p.m. and arrives in Delhi at 2:05 p.m. the following day. Via its Delhi hub, Air India offers onward connections to Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Chandigarh, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Kochi.

Premium Economy Arrives in Canada

The new Boeing 787-9 features a three-class configuration with 30 Business Class private suites, 28 Premium Economy seats, and 238 Economy seats. The aircraft are line-fit — meaning the cabin interiors were installed during production rather than retrofitted — according to Aviation A2Z.

Premium Economy, making its Canadian debut on the route, offers a 2-3-2 seating layout with 38-inch seat pitch, adjustable headrests and leg rests, and 13.3-inch 4K entertainment screens. Business Class passengers get private suites with direct aisle access, 79-inch lie-flat beds, wireless charging, and 17-inch 4K screens.

Across all cabins, the Thales AVANT Up entertainment system provides more than 3,000 hours of content with Bluetooth audio connectivity. USB-A, USB-C, and AC power outlets are standard. The airline has also introduced mood lighting inspired by Indian wellness traditions, refreshed menus with Indian and international cuisine, redesigned amenity kits, and upgraded bedding.

Part of a Massive Fleet Overhaul

The Toronto deployment fits into Air India's sweeping fleet renewal, which encompasses orders for 600 new Airbus and Boeing aircraft — among the largest single airline orders in aviation history. The carrier has taken delivery of three Boeing 787-9s over the past six months, with additional 787-9s and Airbus A350-1000s expected later this year.

Air India is simultaneously retrofitting its existing widebody fleet. Two Boeing 787-8 aircraft with refreshed interiors have returned to service, with three more undergoing upgrades in the United States. The airline expects more than half of its widebody fleet to carry new or upgraded cabins by the end of 2026, according to Travelweek.

The broader summer 2026 deployment plan also includes new 787-9 and retrofitted 787-8 aircraft on Mumbai and Bengaluru routes to London Heathrow, and upgraded 777-300ERs on Delhi-Melbourne service with a new First Class cabin. With the Toronto upgrade, more than 50 percent of Air India's North America flights will operate with new or upgraded cabin interiors.

What It Means for India-Canada Travellers

For the roughly 1.9 million people of Indian origin living in Canada — one of the largest Indian diaspora populations globally — the upgrade addresses longstanding complaints about aging cabin products and indirect routing on the corridor. The elimination of the Vienna stop alone makes the westbound journey substantially more competitive with rival carriers operating nonstop between Indian cities and Toronto.

The introduction of Premium Economy also fills a gap between full-fare business class and economy, offering travellers on the 17-hour flight a middle option that has become standard on most competing long-haul services.
